requirements.quote: Stream flow control, which prevents a single stream from consuming the entire receive buffer for a connection by limiting the amount of data that can be sent on each stream.
requirements.condition: When sending data on an individual stream
requirements.required_behavior: Limit the amount of data sent on that stream according to its stream flow-control limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Allow a single stream to send beyond its stream flow-control limit.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation can track bytes or offsets sent per stream and compare them with that stream's advertised limit.

requirements.quote: Connection flow control, which prevents senders from exceeding a receiver's buffer capacity for the connection by limiting the total bytes of stream data sent in STREAM frames on all streams.
requirements.condition: When sending stream data in STREAM frames across a connection
requirements.required_behavior: Limit the total stream data sent across all streams according to the connection flow-control limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send aggregate stream data beyond the connection flow-control limit.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation can aggregate the relevant stream offsets or bytes across all streams and compare the result with the connection limit.

requirements.quote: Senders MUST NOT send data in excess of either limit.
requirements.condition: When a stream flow-control limit applies
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send data beyond the applicable stream flow-control limit.
requirements.why_checkable: Sent stream offsets can be compared directly with the advertised stream limit.

requirements.quote: Senders MUST NOT send data in excess of either limit.
requirements.condition: When a connection flow-control limit applies
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send aggregate stream data beyond the advertised connection flow-control limit.
requirements.why_checkable: The aggregate sent stream data can be compared directly with the advertised connection limit.

requirements.quote: A receiver sets initial limits for all streams through transport parameters during the handshake (Section 7.4).
requirements.condition: During the handshake
requirements.required_behavior: Set the initial flow-control limits for all streams through transport parameters.
requirements.why_checkable: Handshake transport parameters and the resulting initial per-stream limits are observable in an implementation or protocol trace.

requirements.quote: Subsequently, a receiver sends MAX_STREAM_DATA frames (Section 19.10) or MAX_DATA frames (Section 19.9) to the sender to advertise larger limits.
requirements.condition: After initial limits have been established and the receiver advertises a larger stream limit
requirements.required_behavior: Use a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame to advertise the larger stream limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace can verify that post-handshake stream-limit increases are conveyed using MAX_STREAM_DATA frames.

requirements.quote: Subsequently, a receiver sends MAX_STREAM_DATA frames (Section 19.10) or MAX_DATA frames (Section 19.9) to the sender to advertise larger limits.
requirements.condition: After initial limits have been established and the receiver advertises a larger connection limit
requirements.required_behavior: Use a MAX_DATA frame to advertise the larger connection limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace can verify that post-handshake connection-limit increases are conveyed using MAX_DATA frames.

requirements.quote: A receiver can advertise a larger limit for a stream by sending a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame with the corresponding stream ID.
requirements.condition: When advertising a larger limit for a particular stream
requirements.required_behavior: Send a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame containing the corresponding stream ID.
requirements.why_checkable: The stream associated with a limit increase can be compared with the stream ID encoded in the frame.

requirements.quote: A MAX_STREAM_DATA frame indicates the maximum absolute byte offset of a stream.
requirements.condition: When interpreting or generating a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the frame's limit as the stream's maximum absolute byte offset.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Interpret the value as a relative increment or as a non-offset byte count.
requirements.why_checkable: Frame processing can be tested against absolute stream offsets and retransmission or overlap scenarios.

requirements.quote: A receiver can advertise a larger limit for a connection by sending a MAX_DATA frame, which indicates the maximum of the sum of the absolute byte offsets of all streams.
requirements.condition: When interpreting or generating a MAX_DATA frame
requirements.required_behavior: Treat its value as the maximum permitted sum of the absolute byte offsets of all streams.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Interpret its value as a per-stream limit or as a relative increment.
requirements.why_checkable: The MAX_DATA value can be compared with the sum of absolute offsets maintained across streams.

requirements.quote: A receiver maintains a cumulative sum of bytes received on all streams, which is used to check for violations of the advertised connection or stream data limits.
requirements.condition: As stream data is received
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain cumulative received-data accounting across streams and use flow-control accounting to check advertised connection and stream limits.
requirements.why_checkable: Internal accounting or focused traces can verify that received data updates limit checks across streams.

requirements.quote: Once a receiver advertises a limit for the connection or a stream, it is not an error to advertise a smaller limit, but the smaller limit has no effect.
requirements.condition: When a receiver advertises a connection or stream limit smaller than one it previously advertised
requirements.error_behavior: Do not treat the smaller-limit advertisement as an error.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can deliver a decreased limit and observe whether the endpoint raises an error.

requirements.quote: Once a receiver advertises a limit for the connection or a stream, it is not an error to advertise a smaller limit, but the smaller limit has no effect.
requirements.condition: When a receiver advertises a connection or stream limit smaller than one it previously advertised
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the previously effective higher limit unchanged.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Reduce the effective flow-control limit to the newly advertised smaller value.
requirements.why_checkable: The effective limit before and after a decreased advertisement can be compared.

requirements.quote: A receiver MUST close the connection with an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR if the sender violates the advertised connection or stream data limits; see Section 11 for details on error handling.
requirements.condition: If the sender violates an advertised connection data limit
requirements.error_behavior: Use an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can send data beyond the connection limit and verify both connection closure and the reported error type.

requirements.quote: A receiver MUST close the connection with an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR if the sender violates the advertised connection or stream data limits; see Section 11 for details on error handling.
requirements.condition: If the sender violates an advertised stream data limit
requirements.error_behavior: Use an error of type FLOW_CONTROL_ERROR.
requirements.why_checkable: A peer can send data beyond a stream limit and verify both connection closure and the reported error type.

requirements.quote: A sender MUST ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frames that do not increase flow control limits.
requirements.condition: When a MAX_STREAM_DATA frame does not increase the applicable stream flow-control limit
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the frame and preserve the existing effective stream limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply a non-increasing MAX_STREAM_DATA value as a new effective limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A non-increasing MAX_STREAM_DATA frame can be injected and the effective stream limit observed.

requirements.quote: A sender MUST ignore any MAX_STREAM_DATA or MAX_DATA frames that do not increase flow control limits.
requirements.condition: When a MAX_DATA frame does not increase the connection flow-control limit
requirements.required_behavior: Ignore the frame and preserve the existing effective connection limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Apply a non-increasing MAX_DATA value as a new effective limit.
requirements.why_checkable: A non-increasing MAX_DATA frame can be injected and the effective connection limit observed.

requirements.quote: If a sender has sent data up to the limit, it will be unable to send new data and is considered blocked.
requirements.condition: When a sender has sent data up to the applicable flow-control limit
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the sender as flow-control blocked and refrain from sending new data governed by that limit.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send new data beyond the exhausted limit.
requirements.why_checkable: Sender state and emitted data can be observed after its sent offset reaches the active limit.

requirements.quote: A sender SHOULD send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate to the receiver that it has data to write but is blocked by flow control limits.
requirements.condition: When the sender has data to write but is blocked by a stream flow-control limit
requirements.required_behavior: Send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate the blocked condition to the receiver.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust a stream limit while retaining queued data and observe whether STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED is sent.

requirements.quote: A sender SHOULD send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate to the receiver that it has data to write but is blocked by flow control limits.
requirements.condition: When the sender has data to write but is blocked by the connection flow-control limit
requirements.required_behavior: Send a DATA_BLOCKED frame to indicate the blocked condition to the receiver.
requirements.why_checkable: A test can exhaust the connection limit while retaining queued data and observe whether DATA_BLOCKED is sent.

requirements.quote: To keep the connection from closing, a sender that is flow control limited SHOULD periodically send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame when it has no ack-eliciting packets in flight.
requirements.condition: When the sender is limited by stream flow control and has no ack-eliciting packets in flight
requirements.why_checkable: A timed test can maintain stream-level blocking with no ack-eliciting packets in flight and observe periodic frame emission.

requirements.quote: To keep the connection from closing, a sender that is flow control limited SHOULD periodically send a STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED or DATA_BLOCKED frame when it has no ack-eliciting packets in flight.
requirements.condition: When the sender is limited by connection flow control and has no ack-eliciting packets in flight
requirements.why_checkable: A timed test can maintain connection-level blocking with no ack-eliciting packets in flight and observe periodic frame emission.
